sources.basis: Supports seasonal efficiency and weather compensation concepts. The specific 45/50/55°C SPF values here are illustrative assumptions, not values published by this source.

limits: Annual space heat defaults to design kW × 1,600 equivalent full-load hours; a transparent rough proxy, not an audited annual simulation or EPC-derived demand. Edit annual useful heat when bills/occupancy support a better estimate.
27 p/kWh is an illustrative flat electricity rate, not a quoted tariff or annual price forecast. No solar or time-of-use saving is assumed.

Heating SPF assumptions 3.6 / 3.3 / 3.0 correspond to design flow 45 / 50 / 55°C with weather compensation. Flow is not assumed constant all year. Actual equipment, climate, cycling, defrost and commissioning change performance.

Hot water is separate: 3,000 kWh/year of heat including assumed cylinder losses, SPF 2.5, plus 150 kWh/year auxiliary/backup electricity outside those SPF assumptions. Neither is a measured household quantity.
Costs include electricity for space heating, hot water and the auxiliary allowance. Exclude standing charges, non-heating household electricity, servicing, finance and future tariff changes.
The sensitivity range varies useful heat ±25% and both SPFs ±15%, with auxiliary electricity fixed. It is a scenario range, not a statistical confidence interval.

BUS deduction is shown separately after installation contingency. Eligibility and grant confirmation remain open; switching it off restores the gross amount. No grant is counted as running-cost savings.
radiatorPricingBasis: User instruction: £300 per radiator change, treated as supply and fitting before contingency; editable. Existing heating is assumed in occupied rooms. Unknown output does not imply absence, adequacy at heat-pump temperatures, or an automatic replacement.

lowerGround.observation: Finished lower-ground room with a visible connected radiator. User identifies lower ground as regularly heated living space. Include it in the heated home; exact temperatures, dimensions and outputs remain separately reviewable.
